title: Primitives spacing harmonization and hybrid auto-layout remediation for Figma library
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: The Figma library contains several component primitives (buttons, table rows, chart axes, and data cells) that exhibit inconsistent spacing, a mix of legacy absolute layout frames and newer auto-layout ‘hybrid’ patterns, and token parity issues across density variants. This ticket coordinates an audit, remediation patterns, and a gated publish so downstream product teams receive stable primitives and versioned tokens.

Goals:
- Replace hybrid absolute/auto-layout implementations with consistent, documented auto-layout patterns that support density variants.
- Ensure token parity across all primitives (spacing tokens, semantic sizing tokens, and density variants).
- Fix specific chart axis/padding and table row-height regressions introduced by prior variant reshuffles.
- Add a lightweight QA checklist that runs before Figma library publish and record rollout notes for product designers and engineers.
acceptance_criteria: All button components have a single auto-layout pattern (horizontal stack with gap token) and expose 3 density variants that map to token names: spacing-xs, spacing-sm, spacing-md.

Table row primitives use constrained auto-height with a min-height token and a stable vertical padding token; existing product pages using table rows show no layout regressions after switching to updated library components.
Chart axis group uses consistent axis-padding token; visual diffs for 5 canonical chart examples show <=1px deltas except where token-driven changes are intentional.
A short remediation doc exists (Confluence) that lists changed component keys, migration steps, and automated find/replace suggestions for affected files referencing old layer names.
Figma library publish passes the QA checklist (token checks, variant counts, no mixed absolute/autolayout frames) and the publish is tagged with release: design-2026.03.1.
Design review and engineering sign-off comments are recorded on the ticket and follow-up engineering work (if required) is linked as dependencies.
notes: Discovery: During the last token swap we introduced a handful of components that retained absolute frames inside auto-layout parents. These cause suspicious pixel shifts when density tokens change.

Trade-offs: Converting every nested absolute frame to proper auto-layout might slightly change visual rendering in a few product-specific canvases; we will provide a migration mapping and a rollback plan.
Pattern decision: Adopt a small set of primitive recipes (HorizontalStack-Button, Row-TablePrimitive, Chart-AxisGroup) with explicit token mapping. Document recipes in the library README.
Sequencing: 1) Audit and list all offenders, 2) Apply automated and manual fixes in a staging file, 3) Run visual QA on canonical examples, 4) Publish behind a gated release with notes.
Engineers to consult: frontend-component-team@redwood.com for token name mapping; platform-infra for any automation around publishing tagging.
Risk: Medium — improper token mapping can cause layout regressions in high-density tables used by billing and logs pages. We'll coordinate with product owners for quick rollback if needed.
